questions.stem: This peripheral blood smear is from a patient with acute myeloid leukemia. What morphologic feature best identifies the large arrowed cells as myeloblasts rather than mature leukocytes?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A bilobed nucleus filled with bright eosinophilic granules

choices.label: B
choices.text: Abundant granular cytoplasm with a segmented multilobed nucleus

choices.label: C
choices.text: A small round condensed nucleus with scant clear cytoplasm

choices.label: D
choices.text: A high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio with fine chromatin and visible nucleoli

choices.label: E
choices.text: Densely clumped chromatin with no discernible nucleoli

explanation.summary: Blasts are the earliest, most immature precursor cells. Myeloblasts are large with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine (open) chromatin, and prominent nucleoli, distinguishing them from the smaller, mature lymphocyte with its condensed nucleus and scant cytoplasm.
explanation.whyCorrect: Blasts are the earliest, most immature precursor cells. Myeloblasts are large with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, fine (open) chromatin, and prominent nucleoli, distinguishing them from the smaller, mature lymphocyte with its condensed nucleus and scant cytoplasm.

questions.stem: The left centrifuged specimen is from a leukemia patient with a WBC count over 600,000/microL; the right is from a healthy donor. What accounts for the markedly expanded middle layer in the patient's sample?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A massive increase in circulating white blood cells

choices.label: C
choices.text: A large rise in plasma protein concentration

choices.label: D
choices.text: A marked excess of platelets alone

choices.label: E
choices.text: An expansion of the red blood cell mass (polycythemia)

explanation.summary: When centrifuged, blood separates into plasma, a buffy coat of WBCs and platelets, and red cells. Hyperleukocytosis in acute leukemia grossly expands the buffy (WBC/platelet) layer compared with the thin normal band seen in the healthy donor's blood.
explanation.whyCorrect: When centrifuged, blood separates into plasma, a buffy coat of WBCs and platelets, and red cells. Hyperleukocytosis in acute leukemia grossly expands the buffy (WBC/platelet) layer compared with the thin normal band seen in the healthy donor's blood.
